title: Integer Cache Range
code:
a = 256
b = 256
print(a is b)

a = 257
b = 257
print(a is b)

bugs.fix: print(a == b)  # always use == for value equality
bugs.explanation: CPython caches small integers (-5 to 256), so `256 is 256` is `True`. Integers outside that range are new objects, so `257 is 257` may be `False` (implementation-dependent). Never use `is` to compare integer values — always use `==`.

title: copy.copy vs copy.deepcopy
code:
import copy

orig = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
shallow = copy.copy(orig)
deep = copy.deepcopy(orig)

shallow[0].append(99)
print(orig)   # modified
print(deep)   # not modified

title: __slots__ vs __dict__ Memory
code:
class A:
    def __init__(self, x): self.x = x

class B:
    __slots__ = ('x',)
    def __init__(self, x): self.x = x

import sys
print(sys.getsizeof(A(1)))
print(sys.getsizeof(B(1)))

title: Circular Reference and gc
code:
import gc

class Node:
    def __init__(self): self.ref = None

a = Node()
b = Node()
a.ref = b
b.ref = a
del a, b
gc.collect()

title: String Immutability
code:
s = 'hello'
s[0] = 'H'

bugs.explanation: Strings in Python are immutable. Item assignment (`s[0] = 'H'`) raises `TypeError: 'str' object does not support item assignment`. Create a new string instead: `s = 'H' + s[1:]`.

title: Enum Value vs Name
code:

class Status(Enum):
    ACTIVE = 1
    INACTIVE = 2

print(Status(1).name)
print(Status['ACTIVE'].value)

title: Bitwise Flags With IntFlag
code:
from enum import IntFlag

class Perm(IntFlag):
    READ = 1
    WRITE = 2
    EXEC = 4

perm = Perm.READ | Perm.WRITE
print(perm)
print(bool(perm & Perm.READ))

title: Deleting During Iteration

bugs.explanation: Modifying a dict while iterating over it raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. Convert the keys to a list first with `list(d)` to iterate over a static snapshot.
